subject: Pilot request: temporary dedicated slice + autoscale exception for EchoHealth
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@echohealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot request: temporary dedicated slice + autoscale exception for EchoHealth

Team —

EchoHealth is ready to start their 2-week pilot next Monday (Jul 26). They want to run our mid-size instruction-tuned model with sequence lengths around 1k tokens for clinical summarization demos. Key asks from the customer:
- A dedicated slice (pre-warmed) equivalent to ~4 A100s for predictable latency during demo windows
- A temporary autoscale allowance to burst up to 2x for short evaluation spikes (no more than 6 hours total across pilot)
- Basic telemetry (p50/p95 latency, token cost) surfaced in a shared runbook

Estimated steady QPS: 8–12 across peak hours, peak bursts up to ~25 QPS. Rough token volume: ~120k tokens/day projected.

Can infra/ops confirm whether we can carve a temporary pool for Jul 26–Aug 8 and grant an autoscale exception bounded by a hard budget cap? I attached the pilot SOW and our usage estimates.

Customer contact: Alex Ramos (cloudops@echohealth.com). They're checking SOC2 checklist, but control plane access won't be requested for the pilot.

Asks:
- @karthik_iyer: feasibility + any constraints for autoscale policy exceptions
- @marcus_lin: telemetry knobs and dashboards we should wire up before go-live
- @kimberly_park: commercial guardrails (billing model for this reserved-slice + burst) and confirmation from customer on billing acceptance
- @dev_patel: ops runbook + playbook for fallback to hosted CPU-only path if capacity issues arise

Thanks — aiming to lock this down by EOD Friday so the infra tickets can be provisioned.

—
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments: EchoHealth_Pilot_SOW.pdf; usage-estimates.xlsx

Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary dedicated slice + autoscale exception for EchoHealth

Thanks Ava — quick clarifying items from the commercial side:

1) Duration: you said Jul 26–Aug 8 (13 days). Confirming that's correct; customer will accept a flat pilot fee + overage billing if they exceed the budget cap?
2) Budget cap: what hard $ cap should we set for the autoscale exception so we can get explicit customer sign-off?
3) SLA/gating: do we need to guarantee p95 latency targets for the demo? If so, we should spell that out in the pilot SOW.

Alex — can you confirm budget acceptance and whether EchoHealth expects Redwood to cover any overage during this short eval?

If commercial is good, I'll draft a short addendum to the SOW that captures the slice size, burst allowance, and billing terms.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary dedicated slice + autoscale exception for EchoHealth

On Fri, Jul 23, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> EchoHealth is ready to start their 2-week pilot next Monday (Jul 26)...

Quick infra readout: the request is feasible but has a few caveats. Summary of technical points and recommended plan:

1) Dedicated slice: we can reserve 4 A100-equivalent instances for the window with pre-warm (~30m spin-up) if we create the reservation by EOD Fri. That will ensure stable latency.

2) Autoscale exception: I do not recommend an open burst policy. Instead:
   - Approve a timeboxed burst allowance (2x) with a cumulative burst budget (e.g., 6 hours total) enforced by the quota engine.
   - Implement a hard spend cap at the infra layer that prevents runaway overage (we can flip to strict throttling once budget exhausted).

3) Routing & fallback: configure a fallback policy that routes overflow to a smaller compatible model variant to preserve availability if the slice reaches cap. We should also enable prefix/KV caching for the typical clinical templates to reduce token cost during demos.

4) Telemetry: Marcus can wire p50/p95 + token counts into a shared dashboard. I'll add traces for any cold-starts during the first 48 hours.

Operational asks for provisioning: exact region (us-west-2?), confirmation of the model variant name, and a signed addendum with the agreed hard cap. Also need a ticket in Jira so ops can track provisioning and the runbook.

I'll open the infra reservation once commercial signs off.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@echohealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-26T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary dedicated slice + autoscale exception for EchoHealth

+1 on Karthik's plan. Operational checklist I'm proposing for the pilot (I'll draft the runbook and post to the Drive link):

- Provision reservation in us-west-2: 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes, pre-warmed at 30m before the first demo slot.
- Quota rule: 2x burst allowed, cumulative 6 hours, enforced by quota engine with auto-throttle when spent.
- Spend cap: set at $6,000 for the pilot window (adjustable if sales/customer requests).
- Fallback policy: overflow routes to smaller model (redwood-midsize-v2) with a hard throttle guard.
- Observability: Marcus to enable dashboard and a short Slack alert channel #pilot-echohealth for p95 breaches > 500ms or spend > 80% cap.
- Runbook steps: smoke test, pre-warm checks, rollback (route to hosted API), contact list.

Attachments: draft runbook attached (echohealth-runbook-draft.md). I'll create Jira INFRA-2197 and add checklist tasks.

—
Dev Patel
SRE | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — summarizing agreed approach so we have a single source of truth before provisioning: 

- Pilot window: Jul 26–Aug 8 (inclusive).
- Reservation: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2, pre-warmed for demo windows.
- Autoscale allowance: 2x burst, capped at 6 cumulative hours; infra will auto-throttle on cap exhaustion.
- Spend cap: $6,000 for the pilot (EchoHealth confirms they accept this; Alex please reply to this thread to confirm).
- Fallback: route traffic to redwood-midsize-v2 when reservation is exhausted.
- Observability: Marcus to share dashboard link and Dev will post the runbook to the Drive link in related_links.

Next steps: Kimberly to produce SOW addendum capturing the billing terms and obtain EchoHealth sign-off. Karthik/Dev to open INFRA-2197 and provision once signed addendum is returned. Target: reservation created 24 hours after signed addendum.

Alex — please confirm budget acceptance and I will kick off the addendum.
